narrative.overview:
The page is a public-works poster pulled in flat inks on buff stock, after the 1936-43 Federal Art Project posters for public programs. Each ink is a fixed meaning, not a decoration: orange is Elon Musk's money, blue is the 400 richest Americans' money and the familiar amounts that set the scale, key ink is everything else drawn to scale, and bare stock is paper with nothing printed on it. When a program is funded, its ink is cut away and the stock shows through. The scale is the argument, so the system's first job is to leave every drawn area exactly the size its dollars say.

Density is poster density: one idea per stop, solid poster capitals (Big Shoulders Display) that shout, Public Sans that reads, and long stretches of solid ink the reader scrolls through to feel a sum. The cut stencil survives only as decoration, on the title poster and the FUNDED stamp; the direction contract named stencil capitals for headings, and the build moved them to the solid face. Every bar carries a printed ruler of $100 million sections, and when the reader stops, a grid of one hundred $1 million squares prints over the section at the left edge. There is no elevation, no gradient lighting, no rounded card. Depth is only ink over stock, and the one sanctioned misregistration (orange pulled under the key ink) on the title and the ending poster.
keyCharacteristics: Six inks, each with one job; gold is reserved for "now".
$1,000 per square pixel wherever money is drawn; rulers mark $100 million every 200px.
Solid poster capitals (Big Shoulders Display 900) for headings, bar labels, figures, tabs and counters; Big Shoulders Stencil only for the title poster and the FUNDED stamp; Public Sans for reading.
Every amount's label sits above its shape, in ink on stock.
Square corners everywhere; the pie is the only round shape.
The knock-out: a program's blue is cut back to bare stock as the reader passes, and the pie loses the same slice.
Charts and photos sit in windows of bare stock; nothing is lifted with a shadow.

rules.name: The One Ink, One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Orange is Musk's money; blue is the 400's money, net worth, and the familiar amounts that set the scale; key ink is earnings and every other amount drawn to scale. Do not reassign a bar's ink for variety.

rules.name: The Reserved Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold (#c9a227) appears only for "now": the in-progress pie slice, the reading mark, and `::selection`. Focus rings are ink on a stock halo, because gold fails 3:1 on stock and orange. A finished state is never gold; a funded slice goes to stock.

rules.name: The Pulled Stamp Rule
rules.body: Marks and text on bare stock that want orange use Cancellation Orange (#b4441a), never Musk Orange.

rules.name: The Ink Pairing Rule
rules.body: Key ink on orange; stock on blue and on ink fields; blue or ink on stock. Charts and photos never sit directly on a bar: they sit in a stock window.

rules.name: The Capitals Shout, Sans Explains Rule
rules.body: Poster capitals are uppercase and weight 900, for names, labels, figures, tabs and counters. Sentences and sources are Public Sans. Never set a paragraph in poster capitals.

rules.name: The Stencil Is Decoration Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders Stencil prints only the title poster and the FUNDED stamp. Every other heading, label, figure and tab is Big Shoulders Display.

rules.name: The One Big Number Rule
rules.body: Each program carries exactly one Figure-size number, its cost, and the label window always holds the whole number (`width: max-content`, no wrap).

rules.name: The Lining Figures Rule
rules.body: Body numerals are lining; anything that counts (the strip) uses tabular numerals so it does not jitter.

rules.name: The Scale Is Sacred Rule
rules.body: A drawn money shape's area is its dollars divided by 1,000, in pixels. Changing a number means changing its drawn size; no style may change a drawn size.

rules.name: The No New Width Rule
rules.body: Nothing in a bar's flex row changes width at runtime, and nothing adds page width. Animate paint (gradients, opacity, transforms of non-flow marks), never width.

rules.name: The Clear Zone Rule
rules.body: On screens wider than 450px, the left 250px of a bar hold only the ruler, the key marker, the bar's own label and the $100 million grid. Box figures start at 250px; text and charts center to its right.

rules.name: The Flat Ink Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows or elevation on any element. If something needs separating, put it in a stock window or an ink field.

rules.name: The Overprint Rule
rules.body: The orange misregistration belongs only to Display-size headings, at most two on the page. It is a print artifact, not a shadow style.

dos: **Do** draw every amount at $1,000 per square pixel: bars 500px tall, money bars 400px tall at dollars / 400,000 wide, squares sqrt(dollars / 1000) on a side ($1 million = 31.62px).
**Do** paint program bars with the stock-to-blue gradient driven by `--cut`; change paint, never width.
**Do** keep gold (#c9a227) for "now" only: the in-progress slice, the reading mark, text selection.
**Do** use Cancellation Orange (#b4441a) for stamps and marks on bare stock, and only at stamp or bold-mark size.
**Do** set key ink on orange, stock on blue and on ink fields, and put charts and photos in stock windows with 16px padding.
**Do** set headings, bar labels, figures, tabs and counters in Big Shoulders Display 900 uppercase, and reading text in Public Sans.
**Do** put every amount's label above its shape, in key ink on stock.
**Do** keep the left 250px of a bar clear on screens wider than 450px: box figures at 250px, text and charts centered on calc(50% + 125px), widths capped at calc(100vw − 310px).
**Do** measure bars with the $100 million ruler (200px sections) and land Back/Next stops inside a bar on its ticks.
**Do** give each figure a printed source line (dateline) in 13-14px Public Sans.
donts: **Don't** let anything in a bar's flex row change width at runtime, and don't add page width; the page is about 17.82 million px wide, near Firefox's limit.
**Don't** draw non-money quantities (deaths, people) on the bars as money shapes; they go in the strip or in stock windows.
**Don't** use gold for a finished state, a decoration, or a category color.
**Don't** put Musk Orange text or thin marks on bare stock (2.77:1).
**Don't** add drop shadows, rounded corners, or gradient lighting; the overprint stays on Display-size headings only.
**Don't** use Big Shoulders Stencil for anything but the title poster and the FUNDED stamp.
**Don't** set sentences in poster capitals or headings in Public Sans.
